section_summary.extract_value: This section presents findings from a study examining body size ideals and perceptions among young Black women. The results indicate that participants selected smaller figures to represent their personal ideal body size compared to their perception of ethnic group ideals, and perceived their own body size as smaller than that of typical ethnic female peers, despite over 40% having BMI in the overweight or obese range. The authors discuss these findings through social comparison and self-discrepancy theoretical frameworks.
